item.title: Watford set to appoint former Romania boss Iordanescu
item.description: Edward Iordanescu's most recent job was with Legia Warsaw, who he left in October 2025 [Getty Images] Watford are set to appoint Edward Iordanescu as their new manager. BBC Three Counties Radio report the Romanian is due to become the Hornets' sixth manager inside 18 months after they sacked head coach Alessio Dionisi following Saturday's 4-0 defeat at Sheffield United in his 18th game in charge. The 48-year-old is understood to be arriving in the UK on Tuesday to sign his contract and plans to bring three members of staff with him and hopes to be in the dugout for Wednesday's Championship fixture at home to Blackburn Rovers (19:45 GMT). Iordanescu guided Romania at Euro 2024 where they topped their group ahead of Belgium with all four sides ending level on four points from three games before a 3-0 defeat against the Netherlands in the Round of 16. Iordanescu - whose father Anghel had three spells in charge of the Romanian national team, leading them in two World Cups and two European Championships - left his last role at Polish club Legia Warsaw in October 2025. It was the 48-year-old's ninth club over a 15-year coaching career which has taken in Bulgarian club CSKA Sofia as well as Steaua Bucharest and Cluj among others in his homeland. Dionisi, who departed with the Hornets in 21st, four points above the relegation zone, was only appointed in June after the departure of Ed Still, who himself lasted only three months at Vicarage Road. Still, Javi Gracia and Paulo Pezzolano were all also given full-time contracts after Tom Cleverley left in May 2025. The 46-year-old Italian was Watford's 12th head coach, not including interim bosses, since the end of the 2020-21 season, and leaves the Hornets searching for a 25th since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012. The club have had 57 permanent managers in their 145-year history. Pioneer or coach-eater? item.title: 'My silence should never be mistaken for weakness': Prithvi Shaw warns of legal action
item.description: NEW DELHI: Prithvi Shaw has hit back at former cricketer Yograj Singh over his remarks about the batter's career and personal life. Shaw said he had nothing to hide about his past but would not allow anyone to use it to spread negativity, damage his reputation or gain publicity. Yograj had blamed Shaw's career decline on his lifestyle, including partying, drinking and being in bad company. He also compared the Indian batter's situation with that of former India cricketer Vinod Kambli. "Why did Prithvi Shaw go downhill? It happened with Vinod Kambli before him. It was because of parties, womanising, cigarettes, and drinking. I once asked Kambli, ‘What are you, son?’ You have so much talent," Yograj said on Sports Launchpad. "You are coming to your room at 2.30 in the night. He said, ‘Your days are over, and we’re playing a different kind of cricket now.’ The next morning, Courtney Walsh bowled him, and India lost the match. Then the girl he was with left him, and no one offered him cigarettes and alcohol. The same happened with Shaw. When you go to parties, womanise, drink, and are in bad company, the same will happen to you as happened to them," he added. Shaw warns of legal action Shaw responded to Yograj's comments through a detailed Instagram statement. The batter said he had no issues with his past but would not accept attempts to target him or spread false claims about his personal life. "My past is a part of my life, and I have absolutely nothing to hide or be ashamed of. However, I will not tolerate individuals deliberately using my name, my personal life, or my past to spread negativity, create unnecessary controversy, damage my reputation, or gain publicity and attention at my expense. There is a clear difference between expressing an opinion and deliberately targeting someone with false, misleading, defamatory, or malicious content. Let this be a clear and final warning: Any individual or platform engaging in such activities may face appropriate legal action," Shaw said. The batter also said he was ready to take legal steps to protect his dignity, privacy and reputation. He made it clear that his silence should not be mistaken for weakness. "I reserve the right to pursue all legal remedies available to protect my dignity, privacy, and reputation. My silence should never be mistaken for weakness. I choose to move forward with dignity, but I will not hesitate to stand up for myself," he added. Shaw last represented India in 2021. The 27-year-old has played five Tests, six ODIs and one T20I for India.

item.title: Mendon's title hopes ends in state finals loss to Gaylord St. Mary
item.description: MARQUETTE — The Mendon Hornets have a love-hate relationship with the Superior Dome. Making it all the way north to play in the state finals is certainly an accomplishment. Mendon has done it twice now since moving to the 8-player football divisions of the MHSAA. Northern Michigan University is the host site for the 8-player finals and Mendon has now dropped both games it has played inside the Superior Dome. Despite doing a lot of positive things on Saturday, Mendon came up short in the state championship game. The Hornets faced off against a strong Gaylord St. Mary team and ultimately, the Snowbirds made big plays when it mattered and took advantage of some Mendon miscues. The end result was St. Mary's first state championship in football as the Snowbirds picked up a 49-34 victory in the Division 2, 8-player finals. "We just couldn't get out of our own way at times, we made some mistakes today we hadn't made all year," Mendon coach Bobby Kretschman said. "Sometimes that's gonna happen when you play a good team. I don't wanna take anything away from them. Our kids played hard. We battled the whole game and didn't quit. This was a hell of a lot more fun than when we were here in '22." So for the second time in as many trips to Marquette, the Hornets claimed a trophy – but it was not the one they were in search of at the end of the season. "I'm proud of the kids. I'm proud of everything we accomplished," Kretschman said. "We just fell short today." Both teams came into the contest with records of 12-0 for the year. The Hornets made their way to the finals largely in part to running over everyone in their path. Running the football has always been a staple of Mendon football and this year proved to be more of the same. But St. Mary made big play after big play when it counted. St. Mary led the game 35-34 with just under five minutes remaining in the contest. To get the deficit down to a point, the Hornets scored for the final time on a 4-yard TD rush from Logan Stuart which capped off an 18-play, 80-yard drive for the Hornets which took 7:30 off the clock. St. Mary would answer with the final two touchdowns of the game. They both came from Cal Royce, who had a monster game on both sides of the football. item.title: Little solace - and no Solis - in setback at Stoke
item.description: [BBC] [Press Association] Did the international break come at the wrong time for us? We'd gone into it buoyant after our last-minute victory over Swansea, but we seemed to have lost momentum by the time we got to the Bet365 Stadium on Saturday afternoon. Although August Priske and James Beadle were back from injury, the big miss for me was Jhon Solis. When he isn't available, it makes a significant difference to the way we play. While Paik Seung-ho and Tomoki Iwata in midfield were the go-to pairing during our season in League One, they don't seem to provide enough physical presence in the Championship. In general, Blues were pretty lacklustre; we seemed a bit ring-rusty and while we managed to deal with Stoke's press in the first half, it didn't seem to leave us with much energy for attacking. This extended to us being caught out early in the second half and conceding. Although Chris Davies used most of the attacking options we had on the subs' bench, we just weren't clinical enough to force an equaliser, despite pushing Stoke hard towards the end of the game. Mark Robins is an experienced manager and a wily campaigner, and he had clearly set Stoke up to frustrate our attacking options. Even with Stoke down to 10 men in the second half, he bolstered his defence to hold on to their slender lead. This meeting with Stoke was always likely to be close; we were only separated by goal difference. To be honest, I'd have been happy with a point, but we couldn't find our way to one. However, we're still fourth and need to pick ourselves up ready for a trip to Burnley on Wednesday night. Hopefully, we will have sorted ourselves out by then. It's getting to that time where we need to start thinking about the transfer window again. Given that Marvin Ducksch is likely to be off, does our recruitment team need to think about another strong midfielder to go alongside Solis? He sustained a minor left hamstring issue early in the second set and played with his left thigh heavily strapped. Alcaraz will return to the court at the upcoming Davis Cup, which will be held from November 24-29 at the SuperTennis Arena (BolognaFiere) in Bologna, Italy. The Spaniard is reported to travel from Turin to Bologna by car on Monday, Nov. 23, after winning his first ATP Finals title on Sunday. item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) in the tunnel before game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field. (Eric Hartline-Imagn Images) The Pittsburgh Steelers have plenty to sort through in the film room this week, and Aaron Rodgers has thoughts on how that room ought to run. During the CBS broadcast of Sunday’s 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, reporter Melanie Collins relayed that the veteran quarterback wants more interaction when the team gathers for meetings. “He called for more interaction. He said it’s tough nowadays with these iPads,” Collins said. However, the request didn’t sit well with some fans, who turned the talk of accountability back on the quarterback. Melanie Collins Details Aaron Rodgers’ Point About iPads in Team Meetings The remarks came on a rough afternoon for Pittsburgh. The Steelers dropped to 6-4 with their second straight loss, a week after falling 38-18 in Cincinnati, and Rodgers was sacked five times while the offense converted 5 of 17 third downs. Collins kept going and gave her own read on the quarterback’s tone along the way. “Back in the day, you could check guys’ notes and make sure they were writing things down. It almost felt like he was calling out the guys a little bit for a lack of details. He wants everyone to feel like they’re contributing to what’s happening on game day, even when they’re not on the field.” Some fans decided to turn that call for details back on the quarterback himself. “Dude was overthrowing by a mile. Take some accountability bro,” one said , while another added , “The guy who screams at WRs when he throws it 10 yards over their heads wants more accountability? That’s rich.” Rodgers completed 30 of 44 passes, a 68.2% clip, for 227 yards and a touchdown without an interception Sunday, and his completion percentage over expected of 2.2 ranked 10th of 24 qualified quarterbacks in Week 11. For the season, though, his 60.9% completion rate through Week 11 sits 23rd of 32 qualified quarterbacks, and his 86.6 passer rating is tied for 19th of 32. Pro Football Network’s NFL QB Impact Grade has him at 67 over the same span, 29th of 33 graded quarterbacks. item.title: Napoli visit Man City without 11 players as Vergara faces lengthy layoff
item.description: Napoli visit Man City without 11 players as Vergara faces lengthy layoff Napoli will travel to Manchester City without 11 players, including four centre-backs, while Antonio Vergara is expected to be sidelined for more than two months with a high-grade tear in his left thigh. Napoli face several selection problems ahead of Tuesday’s Champions League away match against Manchester City. The Partenopei, who sit eighth in Serie A, will travel to England without 11 first-team players. NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 20: Massimiliano Allegri, Manager of SSC Napoli, reacts during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between SSC Napoli and FK Bodo/Glimt at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 20, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Alisson Santos, Benoit Badiashile, Alessandro Buongiorno, captain Giovanni Di Lorenzo, Stanislav Lobotka, Alex Meret and David Neres are injured; Rafa Marin is suspended, while Luca Marianucci and Costantino Favasuli are not part of their UEFA squad. Vergara was the latest player to suffer an injury, coming off in the first half of Saturday’s 1-0 win over Torino at the Stadio Maradona. Napoli issued a statement on Monday after the Italy international underwent medical tests. The club said Vergara had suffered a high-grade tear of the right biceps femoris muscle in his left thigh. According to Sky Sport, the 23-year-old is expected to be out for more than two months. NAPLES, ITALY – NOVEMBER 21: Antonio Vergara of SSC Napoli is consoled by teammate Matteo Politano as he is substituted off after sustaining an injury during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Torino FC at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on November 21, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Napoli’s injury crisis has hit hardest in attack and defence. In Manchester, coach Massimiliano Allegri will be without four of his six centre-backs, predictably prompting Mathias Olivera to join Amir Rrahmani and Sam Beukema in a three-man back line. Allegri will hold a pre-match press conference in Manchester later today, alongside former Manchester City star Kevin De Bruyne. NAPLES, ITALY – NOVEMBER 21: Kevin De Bruyne of SSC Napoli is challenged by Rafik Belghali of Torino FC during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Torino FC at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on November 21, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Allegri has already suggested Napoli may not travel to Manchester with their highest motivation. “It’s a very important match and a great one to play in,” the coach said after Saturday’s win over Torino. “We have to be realistic; our Champions League campaign will be decided against Club Brugge, Sabah and Viking. We had to beat Bodo, and we did. Tuesday will be very important and difficult, but we need to sort out the league, and the home match against Club Brugge will be crucial.”

item.title: Marseille manager Bruno Genesio: ‘There is a global phenomenon of fragility as soon as we concede a goal.’
item.description: Marseille manager Bruno Genesio: ‘There is a global phenomenon of fragility as soon as we concede a goal.’ Olympique de Marseille were seemingly in complete control and sauntering towards a victory against Le Mans FC that would have extended their winning run in Ligue 1 to six games. 2-0 up thanks to goals from Amine Gouiri and Igor Paixao, Bruno Genesio’s side were cruising until Louis Mafouta’s direct free-kick, which struck the inside of the post before going in on the 70th minute. That goal instigated a collapse from Marseille. Mafouta then missed a penalty to level the scores, but it was a miss that would ultimately prove inconsequential, with Le Mans securing a spectacular comeback win thanks to Jean Vercruysse’s 95th-minute winner at the Vélodrome. “There is a global phenomenon of fragility as soon as we concede a goal,” reacted Genesio in a post-match press conference attended by Get French Football News. “There are also tactical problems to solve because we are poorly positioned on the goals that we concede […] there are also mental problems that are present sometimes at the ends of matches. Tonight, we were at 100% for 60% of the match and then we were below 100% for 40% of it.” GFFN | Luke Entwistle

This Thursday, they’ll host the Chicago Bears, who also enter this game at 8-2, but are 0-2 in the division, putting them in second place. The Bears opened the season by dropping 59 points on the Panthers and had Johnson talking about setting the NFL scoring record . The next week, the Bears scored only three points in a 9-3 loss to the Vikings. Georgia has already secured a place in the SEC Championship Game. However, the identity of its opponent remains uncertain. Alabama, Texas and Tennessee enter the final weekend competing for the remaining berth, creating a complicated situation involving head-to-head results and conference tiebreakers. And the most interesting part might be that some of the deciding games will not feature the three contenders. The SEC championship race extends beyond the contenders Conference championship races usually come down to whether the leading teams win their final games. However, the SEC’s expanded membership and scheduling format have created a more complicated scenario. When teams finish with identical conference records, the league applies a series of tiebreaking procedures. Those include head-to-head results, records against common opponents and, when necessary, the combined conference winning percentage of opponents. Consequently, games involving teams outside the championship race can become important. The Egg Bowl between Mississippi State and Ole Miss is one matchup that could affect the calculations. item.description: Lee Fryer is due to face trial at Leeds Crown Court next March [Getty Images] An athlete who won a silver medal for Britain at the 2024 Paralympics in Paris has been charged with 11 counts of rape. Wheelchair basketball player Lee Fryer, 26, from Pontefract, West Yorkshire, faces 17 charges in total, including voyeurism, intentional strangulation, assault and possession of a class A drug, namely cocaine. He appeared at Leeds Crown Court on Thursday, where he pleaded not guilty to all the charges except voyeurism, for which no plea was entered. He is due to stand trial on 22 March next year. British Wheelchair Basketball (BWB) confirmed he had been removed from the GB programme and all British Wheelchair Basketball activities when he was arrested in July. Fryer is also charged with controlling or coercive behaviour in an intimate relationship and perverting the course of justice. A BWB spokeperson said: "We are aware of the criminal charges brought against Lee Fryer and recognise the seriousness of the allegations. "At the point of his arrest, he was removed from the GB Programme and all British Wheelchair Basketball activities, pending the outcome of the external investigation. "As criminal proceedings are ongoing, it would be inappropriate to comment further at this time." ParalympicsGB said: "We are aware there are charges against Lee Fryer. item.title: Miami Dolphins news roundup: Reviewing Week 11’s loss to the Buffalo Bills
item.description: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 22: Jacob Rodriguez #10 of the Miami Dolphins intercepts a pass during the second quarter of a game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 22, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins lost to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, falling to 1-9. The Dolphins were outmatched throughout the game, playing tough but not being able to avoid the mistakes and growing pains that come with a rebuild. The Bills took advantage of those issues and put away their AFC East rivals in the first of two games between the clubs this year. Miami leaned on its defense in this game, with linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, edge rusher Chop Robinson, and safety Zayne Anderson all shining in the loss. Miami’s offense struggled to keep up, however, especially with multiple drops from wide receivers Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell; quarterback Kyle McCord, playing in his second game in the NFL, had the up-and-down performance that should be expected of a younger player, throwing some beautiful passes but also showing some inaccuracy and forcing some passes where they should not have been thrown. The Miami special teams were more consistent this week than we have seen in recent games. New kicker Daniel Carlson connected on all three of his field goals, the Dolphins’ only points on Sunday, hitting from 27 yards and twice from 52 yards. Punter Jack Browning, filling in for the injured Bradley Pinion, kicked four times for an average of 41.3 yards. A couple of his punts were only 31 yards, but he also boomed a 50-yarder that could have been downed inside the five-yard line, but the coverage team reacted to the returner signaling for a fair catch and did not realize he was letting the ball go over his head. The Bills have the best record in the NFL, and they played like it on Sunday. The Dolphins have the worst record in the league and, while they play tough and do not quit, they have that record for a reason. This season is about improvement and growth. item.title: Clippers Deliberately Playing Rui Hachimura, Brook Lopez and Other Veterans To Showcase Value Ahead Of Trade Deadline: Report
item.description: Clippers veteran players, including Rui Hachimura, Brook Lopez on trade block © X/@LAClippers The LA Clippers are unlikely to make the playoffs, but they are prioritizing minutes for veteran players – Rui Hachimura, Brook Lopez, Kris Dunn, Derrick Jones Jr., and Max Strus. LA will likely be a heavy seller and is using the time until February to push its veteran role players’ trade values. According to NBA insider Marc Stein, word has already circulated that the Clippers are actively pushing veterans over young players for this reason. “Strus ($16.7 million), Jones ($10.5 million), Lopez ($9.2 million) and Kris Dunn ($5.7 million) are all on expiring contracts,” Stein wrote for The Stein Line (h/t APHoops). “Hachimura signed a two-year, $28 million contract with the Clippers in the offseason but next season’s $14 million salary is a team option … This is one of the few teams league-wide that is regarded as a certain seller between now and the Feb. 11 trade deadline.” The Clippers hinted at a rebuild last year when they traded Ivica Zubac and James Harden. Kawhi Leonard’s future was in doubt due to contradicting reports. Eventually, the Clippers traded him to Toronto. However, LA still retained most of its supporting cast, which was suitable to compete for the playoffs. The team also signed other veterans, but those moves were for future trades so the Clippers could get draft assets in return after the NBA stripped them of multiple first-round picks through 2033 for cap circumvention in September for illegal payments to Kawhi Leonard ( via ESPN ). Clippers Playing It Perfectly, As Rui Hachimura, Brook Lopez Have Numbers To Back Up Their Favorable Contracts The LA Clippers are playing their cards right this season by giving Rui Hachimura and Brook Lopez bigger roles. Both are on expiring contracts (Hachimura is a team option that can be declined), so they are already on favorable contracts. To draw more value, their roles have led to impressive production. Lopez is the team’s second-best scorer, averaging 15.7 points on 55.2% shooting, including 42.2% from 3. Centers who can shoot that well are already limited, and with numbers like these, the Clippers will likely find it easiest to find bidders who can meet their demands for Lopez. Meanwhile, Hachimura is averaging 14.0 ppg and 6.2 rpg on 40.8% 3-point shooting. Any contender would love to have a big wing who can shoot at a high clip off the bench. Max Strus, Kris Dunn and Derrick Jones Jr. have also been solid. Strus is averaging 9.1 ppg and 3.4 apg, shooting 35.7% from 3. Dunn remains one of the best defensive point guards, averaging 7.0 ppg, 4.1 apg, and 2.0 spg, shooting 45.8% from the field. Jones has probably been at par or even better than Hachimura, averaging 10.3 ppg and 4.5 rpg, shooting 50.1%, including 48.1% from 3. He’s also a better defender than Hachimura. item.title: What's next for Mets this offseason after Tarik Skubal joins team
item.description: Is Flushing now a destination for free agents across Major League Baseball? The Mets' home might have become just that on Sunday night as they reportedly landed Tarik Skubal on a nine-year, $450 million deal that set the new record for a pitcher. The club now has one of baseball's preeminent aces, one of its most elite bats in Juan Soto, a heart of the lineup that also includes Francisco Lindor and Bo Bichette and a captivating young core led by Nolan McLean, Carson Benge and A.J. Ewing. That talent alone — and the championship vision that comes with it — should be an alluring option for players across the league. With Steven Cohen flexing his financial might once again, players know that ownership is going to back up their lofty expectations with action. Now, the Mets head into an uncertain winter, with MLB's owners and the Major League Baseball Players Association negotiating the next labor agreement, with the top prize of free agency already locked up. While the Mets addressed their biggest need atop the starting rotation on Sunday, there is still some shopping that needs to be done before next season can begin. Here are three more needs that the Mets have to address before the 2027 season: Bring in a right-handed first baseman Mets president of baseball operations David Stearns made it clear during MLB's GM meetings that the first base position was a spot where the club would like to add during the offseason. Despite Jared Young proving he was capable of being a regular contributor at the major league level a season ago, the left-handed hitter was much more effective against right-handed pitching (.793 OPS) versus left-handed pitchers (.606 OPS). Beyond Young, there are questions about Mark Vientos' consistency and glove and Jorge Polanco's health and efficacy at the position. A right-handed option should be sought to bring more comfort at the position. If the Mets have the capacity to make another splash, Ty France could fit the bill. Or a less flashy platoon option exists in a veteran like Paul Goldschmidt. Add another capable starting pitcher to the rotation While the Mets have their ace to lead the starting staff, there is still some uncertainty about who will fill out the bottom of the rotation. They have bounce-back candidates in Kodai Senga and Sean Manaea, who have each struggled in back-to-back seasons, Tylor Megill returning from Tommy John surgery and Jonah Tong who could be looking to make more progress after a few spot starts the last few seasons. There could also be options at the minor league level in Jonathan Santucci or Jack Wenninger. But with so many lingering questions, it could make sense to add another dependable arm with fewer questions. Whether that comes from the next class of free agent starters, like Clay Holmes or Nick Martinez, or someone further down the pecking order and less costly, would be the question. item.title: Patrick Mahomes says there’s one thing Travis Kelce does that makes leading Kansas City Chiefs ‘easy’
item.description: Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After 10 years together, Patrick Mahomes reveals one amazing quality of Travis Kelce. The Kansas City Chiefs continue to dominate during the 2026-27 NFL season as they recently registered an easy 34-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals. The Chiefs have now improved to an 8-2 record with the dynamic duo of Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce looking unstoppable in their 10th season together. While much has been said about Mahomes playing well, the star QB recently broke down how Kelce makes his life easier on the field. Patrick Mahomes applauds Travis Kelce’s phenomenal work ethic At 37, there’s a general understanding in the NFL community that this is Kelce’s final season in the league. It could be true, but for now, Mahomes isn’t worried about that. Instead, the Chiefs QB explained one thing that the veteran TE does that makes it ‘easy’ for him to lead the team. “That’s Travis. You can’t take that dude off the football field; he loves it. He goes out there and has success when he plays because he loves it that much to compete, and he’s going to do whatever it takes to help the team win,” Mahomes said. “He made a couple of big plays for us, especially in the early part of the game, and that’s the type of leader he is. I always say it makes my job as a QB easy,” he continued. “… He’s a Hall of Famer and he’s the one that wants to get in there every single rep, that kind of gives you the mindset to tell the other guys, ‘Hey, y’all want to take a rep off? Look at this guy.’ It’s just easy for me as a leader to have someone like that on my team,” the Chiefs QB concluded. Kelce may have played more than 200 games in the NFL, but his hunger to improve every day is what makes him so dangerous on the football field. item.title: Arsenal goalkeeper Raya absent from training session
item.description: Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya leaves the pitch in pain after injuring his shoulder in the match against Newcastle (ANDY BUCHANAN) Goalkeeper David Raya was absent from Arsenal's open training session on Monday ahead of their Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund after he was forced off during the Gunners' 2-2 draw at Newcastle. Understudies Kepa Arrizabalaga and Frenchman Illan Meslier took part in the workout as the players were put through their paces ahead of Tuesday's home match against the Bundesliga side. Raya was replaced by Arrizabalaga in the 70th minute at St James' Park on Saturday after an apparently innocuous collision with Newcastle striker William Osula. The 31-year-old left the pitch clutching his left arm in visible discomfort with an apparent shoulder problem. Raya played a key role as Arsenal ended a 22-year wait for a Premier League title last season and had started this campaign with seven clean sheets in 10 matches before the match in Newcastle. Raya's injury came on the day Arsenal welcomed back William Saliba to the matchday squad. The France defender, who was an unused substitute, has not played this season because of an injury. Winger Bukayo Saka, who has been absent since October 21 due to a thigh injury, is still weeks away from a return. item.title: Chelsea striker Emmanuel Emegha robbed after Leeds thrashing
item.description: Emmanuel Emegha has revealed that he was robbed after Chelsea’s home drubbing by Leeds on Saturday. Emegha started his first Premier League game as the Blues suffered a heavy 4-1 defeat at Stamford Bridge, but was the victim of theft in the hours following the game. The Dutch striker confirmed the incident on Sunday, writing on Instagram: “Unfortunately after the game I was robbed. I am okay and thankfully no one was hurt. Thanks for the messages of support.” Chelsea sources told The Independent that the club is aware of the theft incident involving Emegha and that he has the full support of the club in this matter. The Metropolitan Police have been contacted for comment. Emegha scored his first goal for the Blues against Leeds, brilliantly finishing at the near post to open the scoring in the first half before the tide turned heavily against Chelsea. Noah Okafor equalised three minutes after Emegha’s striker before later scoring again as Leeds ran away with the game after the break, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Brendon Aaronson also netting scoring to condemn Chelsea to a damning loss. Emegha joined Chelsea from sister club Strasbourg in the summer after a deal was agreed to bring the Dutchman to Stamford Bridge in September 2025. He scored 31 goals in 73 appearances across all competitions in his three seasons in France before making the switch.

item.title: SD Huesca, opponent in the second round of the Copa del Rey
item.description: SD Huesca, opponent in the second round of the Copa del Rey Girona FC will visit SD Huesca, an Aragonese team currently competing in the Primera Federación, in the match corresponding to the second round of the 2026/2027 Copa del Rey. The single-elimination match will be played at El Alcoraz between December 1 and 3. SD Huesca currently occupies the 15th position in the Primera Federación, with three wins, six draws, and four losses. In the last matchday, the Aragonese team lost 0-4 to UD Ibiza. The match will also have several points of interest for Girona, with various members of the current Huesca team having a special connection to the Girona club or the region. One of them is Gianfranco Gazzaniga, the goalkeeper of the Aragonese team and brother of Paulo Gazzaniga, Girona's current goalkeeper. On Huesca's bench is Albert Rudé, a coach born in Ripoll in 1987. Rudé took on the role in October after previously managing CD Castellón in the Primera Federación and developing much of his professional career in international football. The Catalan coach has been part of Diego Alonso's technical staff at Pachuca, Monterrey, and Inter Miami, before serving as head coach at Alajuelense in Costa Rica, Castellón, Wisla Kraków, and Kolding IF in Denmark. Cristian Herrera, a forward with a past at Girona, is also part of the team. Herrera wore the red-and-white jersey between January 2016 and the summer of 2017, playing 54 matches and scoring 9 goals with the first team. His time at Montilivi coincided with Girona's historic promotion to La Liga in the 2016/17 season. The Aragonese team also features Óscar Sielva, a footballer born in Olot and the current captain of Huesca. The midfielder from Garrotxa played for UE Olot during the 2014/15 season, appearing in 26 matches and scoring one goal. Sielva later went on to establish a long career in professional football and, since the summer of 2023, has been a permanent member of Huesca's squad. This 2026/27 season, he has participated in eight Primera Federación matches and scored one goal.

item.description: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect Jaden McDaniels made six of his 10 shots against the New York Knicks. Minnesota addressed that before taking the floor again. According to Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic , the Wolves held a long film session Friday focused on offensive adjustments, emphasizing ball movement and getting McDaniels more involved. The instruction sounds simple. Following it requires more than asking McDaniels to become aggressive. item.title: Stay humble, Max? The true sentiments behind Verstappen’s inexorable George Russell tirade
item.description: There’s nothing quite like kicking a man when he’s down. Forlorn once again after a dismal late shunt, George Russell had swiftly completed his media duties and, if he had any sense, was heading straight to Harry Reid International Airport for the first flight back to London when Max Verstappen , gleeful and exuberant after what was undoubtedly a brilliant grand prix win in Las Vegas , entered the FIA press conference room. After 15 minutes of preamble came the bait: Max, was it nice to get one-up on Russell after his remarks – the Briton said Verstappen “screwed him over” and “walks around like he’s bigger and better than everyone else” after a clash in practice which the Dutchman was served an official warning for – on Saturday? Cue Verstappen, vocalising his tried-and-true stream of consciousness. “The thing is… he speaks a lot next to the track,” he said. “And honestly, for me, it doesn’t really bother me because he’s so far below my level that it doesn’t make any sense for me to challenge that.” Max Verstappen: George Russell is ‘so far below my level’ (Getty) He goes on. “And today, karma is a bitch. It was honestly fantastic when I looked in the mirror and I saw what was happening [Russell’s crash]. I was like ‘fantastic, my day is only getting better’ – and then when I crossed the line in first, my day was complete.” Moments earlier, in the TV pen, Verstappen had not needed a leading question in discussion with Dutch broadcaster ViaPlay as he labelled Russell’s season a “complete joke.” Backed up by his victory, swatting Russell’s challenge to the wayside, this was a Verstappen tirade at its most inexorable. As you can imagine, the largely vitriolic world of social media lapped it up. “Tears for George”; “inject this s*** into my veins”; “there’s levels to this game, Max is generational”. And the rest. In one respect, the problem for Russell is that, as per his own words, Verstappen really is better than virtually everyone else on the grid. Only Lewis Hamilton can stake a claim to be in the Dutchman’s sphere of aptitude and, even then, many rate the four-time world champion’s raw talent and pure speed above that of Hamilton. And this is not finishing school; this is elite-level sport. You can immerse yourself in all the mind games and media back-and-forth but, ultimately, your performance dictates everything. You have to back it up. And with his clumsy attempt to pass 20-year-old world champion teammate Kimi Antonelli on the third-last lap and a bump into the barriers, Russell lost a whole load of credibility on Saturday night. For the Briton, now an astonishing 138 points behind Antonelli, it has been nothing short of a disastrous season at the wheel. However, there is still something to be said for a degree of sportsmanship and good grace. And, look: these two clearly don’t get on. Yet even then, rubbing more salt in what is the saltiest of wounds does show a lack of class; a class that is still refreshingly prevalent in other sports. V

item.title: ‘Good for her’: Mark Cuban defends Colts owner’s controversial sideline note-taking
item.description: Carlie Irsay-Gordon watches the action on the field from the Indianapolis Colts sideline Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026, during a game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. Indianapolis Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon has become a regular presence on the team’s sideline during games, often seen wearing a headset and taking notes. And as the Colts have struggled this season, she has faced plenty of criticism for it. But Irsay-Gordon now has a high-profile defender. This week, former Dallas Mavericks owner Mark Cuban came to her defense as he said that Irsay-Gordon is doing exactly what he did during his time in Dallas, and he praised her for caring enough “to not care what other people think.” Irsay-Gordon Faces Criticism Irsay-Gordon took over as the Colts’ principal owner after her father, longtime owner Jim Irsay, died in 2025. Since then, she has taken a hands-on approach on game days, and that hasn’t gone over well with everyone. Back in October, Bill Simmons ripped Irsay-Gordon on his podcast for spending games on the sideline. “I’m not gonna tiptoe around this anymore. And I know it’s been a topic the last couple of weeks; I think the owner on the sidelines taking notes is [freaking] nuts. I think it’s nuts! I think it’s bonkers!” Simmons said. Stephen A. Smith and former Colts quarterback Sean Salisbury have also called her out for being on the sideline. The criticism has only grown louder as the losses have piled up. The Colts fell to 3-8 with a 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans on Thursday night, their fourth defeat in five games. ‘Good for her’ Last week, another clip of Irsay-Gordon taking notes on the sideline made the rounds on social media. Former NFL offensive lineman Mitchell Schwartz came to her defense, and he brought up Cuban, who was famous for sitting right behind the Mavericks’ bench. “I do not get all the hate. She stays out of the way, she listens to the headsets, and she takes notes. In this case she looks up and the coach is nearby and she goes further down the sideline,” Schwartz wrote . “Mark Cuban sat right behind the bench for half a century and no one batted an eye.” Cuban saw the post and explained why he spent all those years sitting behind the bench. “I sat behind the bench for the same reason I sat in on sales and tech meetings. So I could learn. Watching how people interacted. How they responded to the good and bad and each other. Developing closer relationships. Making them comfortable around me so they didn’t think I was a suit in an office and they could talk to me,” Cuban wrote . He added that sitting so close to the action also taught him a lot about the officiating. “I also got to hear what refs said to our coaches and players. And vice versa. Taught me a lot as well. It’s all information to help me make better decisions. The fact that no one else had done it, made it one of the many things I did that other teams didn’t,” Cuban wrote. Cuban then made it clear that he supports Irsay-Gordon.
